messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy attempt for release candidate rc7 failed security gate: vuln-scan found 3 new MEDIUMs and 1 HIGH transitive CVE in dependency chain (pkg:xorg/overlay). Blocked automatically. See /deploy rc7 logs.
marta: ugh. which service? quick link?
deploy-bot: Affected service: inference-frontend:v2. Logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/logs/rc7/1903456789
ash: got it. high is transitive from `libimageproc` used by gpu-utils. we previously accepted it in rc6 via mitigation. new patch changed subdeps.
sam: can we ship a canary without the vulnerable path? maybe disable the optional image preprocessing plugin at runtime and canary 10% traffic.
elaine: @sam that's a good idea if we can toggle via feature flag. but legal asked to avoid known HIGH CVEs in prod even in limited rollout unless there's an approved exception.
sec-eng: to be explicit: policy requires either patch/pin/rollback or a documented, timeboxed exception with compensating controls (WAF rule or feature-flag isolation + monitoring). We can approve an exception for up to 72h for critical shipping windows, but need owner + mitigation + rollback criteria.
marta: timeline: we promised RC7 to customer trial tomorrow morning. if we block, they get delayed. seeking options: 1) patch libimageproc (likely >24h), 2) pin to older transitive that doesn't have CVE (risk of other regressions), 3) exception with canary+feature-flag+runtime guard, 4) full rollback to rc6.
release-manager: decision needed in next 90m to hold or proceed with controlled exception. who will own mitigation/runbook?
sam: I can own the canary route and the runbook. Plan: toggle `IMAGE_PREPROCESS_PLUGIN=false` at startup and route 10% to canary deploy that has plugin disabled. Add WAF rule to block exploit vectors and enable monitoring alerting on anomaly. If no exploitable activity in 72h we can extend or ship final patch.
sec-eng: outline required in thread for approval: owner, mitigation steps, detection metrics, rollback triggers (e.g., CPU spike + 5xx trend or exploit signature), comms plan. postmortem commitment if something goes wrong.
marta: drafting runbook now. I'll paste snippet and checklist.
ash: quick snippet for the flag toggle and canary command:
```
# create canary with plugin disabled
kubectl set env deploy/inference-frontend IMAGE_PREPROCESS_PLUGIN=false -n prod-canary
# route 10% traffic to prod-canary
kubectl apply -f canary-traffic-10pct.yaml
```
sec-eng: add WAF rule id 7482 to block suspicious payloads against /api/v1/transform and enable audit logs. Also add IDS signature for CVE-2026-xxxx (transitive)
elaine: legal: please confirm you accept a 72h exception if sec-eng + release-manager approve and customer is notified. @release-manager
release-manager: legal verbally OK for 72h exception pending formal ticket. we need sec-eng + release-manager + owner signatures in the ticket. I'll open a short-lived Exception Request: EXC-1903 and link it.
marta: EXC-1903 created: https://tickets.redwood/EXC-1903. Runbook + mitigation checklist attached. key items: feature flag toggle, WAF rule, canary 10%, metric dashboards, alert thresholds, rollback command, comms template.
sam: adding rollback commands now and an automated monitor that posts to #incidents if anomaly. Rollback command:
```
# rollback to rc6
kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-frontend --to-revision=rc6 -n prod
kubectl apply -f remove-canary.yaml
```
sec-eng: Approved for exception: sec-eng (sec-eng), release-manager (release-manager), owner (sam). Conditions: 10% canary, WAF rule live, monitor alerts enabled, EXC-1903 ticket open. Exception valid until 72 hours from approval or earlier if patch applied.
elaine: Legal confirmed in ticket comments. Customer notified via account team. Product ops note: feature flag is reversible with no schema changes, safe to rollback.
marta: executing canary now. will post status updates every 15m for first hour.
sam: starting canary: set env + apply traffic split. monitoring: latency/5xx/attack-signature alerts wired to PagerDuty.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy successful: prod-canary up (pod set 3). Traffic split applied.
marta: first 15m: no errors, no signature alerts. CPU stable.
sam: 45m update: still clean. WAF blocked two suspicious requests (blocked by rule 7482). logged and forwarded to sec-eng for analysis.
sec-eng: reviewed blocked requests; looks like automated scanner noise. no exploitation observed. fine to continue.
release-manager: marking EXC-1903 as active and noting approvals. we'll reconvene at 36h to evaluate extension vs patch schedule.
marta: thanks everyone. will post final status before 72h cutoff or earlier if we patch. :thumbsup:
